correctness.rationale: Geometric series give E|X_r|=2r/(1-r²) and endpoint R_B=B/(1+sqrt(1+B²)). For R_B<=sqrt2-1, differentiating log p_r(k) proves every off-center mass is monotone increasing in r, while center decreases; thus total variation mismatch is exactly center-mass difference. The integer-lattice minimum nonzero distance is 1, so for mismatch <1 the Ky–Fan/Prokhorov coupling infimum is the mismatch probability. One-dimensional W1 is the infinite sum of absolute CDF differences and telescopes to the displayed moment difference. Independently checked symbolic identity of the ratio and monotone boundary maximization. The sharp constant is approached by distinct r,s coalescing at R_B; not necessarily attained by distinct pairs. Source finite verifier inspected, not used to prove all parameters.

value.rationale: A sharp benchmark in a natural log-affine discrete distribution family addresses whether the general logarithmic loss is forced even in a canonical unbounded family. It supplies an all-budget exact comparison and universal sharp constant within that family, not an unmotivated single pair or an unsupported removal of log for arbitrary discrete log-concave laws.

final_claim: For centered symmetric geometric laws mu_r(k)=(1-r)/(1+r) r^{|k|} on Z with first absolute moment <=B<=1, exact Levy–Prokhorov and W1 distances between parameters r<s are 2(s-r)/[(1+r)(1+s)] and 2[s/(1-s²)-r/(1-r²)]. Thus their ratio is (1+rs)/[(1-r)(1-s)] and the sharp global comparison constant is 1+B²+B sqrt(1+B²), equal to 2+sqrt2 at B=1.
limitations: Only 0<B<=1, not other crossing regimes, and best sharp constant is a supremum over distinct pairs.
